title: 3.7.4 Lab: Transform a List Without Mutating the Input
description: Use .map() to build a transformed copy of an array, then demonstrate the original is unchanged. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create the source list
steps.instructions: The starter gives you prices, an array of numbers: const prices = [10, 20, 30]; Leave that line as it is.

steps.title: Build a transformed copy with .map()
steps.instructions: Use .map() on prices to build a new array where each number is transformed (for example, doubled), and store the result in a variable called doubled.

steps.title: Log both arrays
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print the transformed array and the original prices array. Confirm the original still holds its starting values.

requirements.title: Array declared
requirements.description: Declares an array with square brackets. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Keep the prices array the starter gives you. It stays as it is.

requirements.title: .map() used
requirements.description: Calls .map() to build a transformed array. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Call .map on prices with a function that changes each number, and keep the result in a second variable.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Print the new array and then prices, so you can see the original did not change.

requirements.title: prices still holds its starting values and both arrays are printed
requirements.description: prices is still [10, 20, 30], doubled holds three transformed numbers, and the output shows them. Help: 3.7.2 (Reading: .map())
requirements.hint: .map() builds a new array and leaves prices alone. Store the result in a second variable and do not assign into prices.

checks.expr: Array.isArray(doubled) && doubled.length === 3 && doubled.some((x, i) => x !== prices[i]) && (J => doubled.every(x => J.includes(String(x))))(output.join(' '))
checks.fail: doubled should hold the three transformed numbers, and your output should show them (and the original prices).
